Master's student in the [Department of Civil Engineering](https://www.civil.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/), Graduate School of Engineering, the University of Tokyo, working in the [Lab for Innovative Infrastructure Systems (Fukuda Lab)](https://liis.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/).
Student of [WINGS-GLAFS](http://www.glafs.u-tokyo.ac.jp/), the University of Tokyo's cross-disciplinary graduate program on aging societies.

**Fields:** Transportation Economics, Urban and Regional Economics

## Research

Japan's population is shrinking and aging.
In this setting, how do investments in and restructuring of transport infrastructure — from high-speed rail to regional railways — change where people choose to live and how well off each region is over the long run?

To answer this question, I develop policy evaluation methods grounded in spatial economics that account for long-run population dynamics, such as migration that unfolds over decades.
Going forward, I aim to extend these methods to capture age structure and finer geographic units, so that they can inform debates such as the future of regional railways.
